items.originalTitle: Getting the most out of Opus 5.5 in Claude and Claude Code
items.summary:
Claude has introduced Opus 5.5, an update designed to enhance performance on extended, multi-step tasks by allowing the model to continue working autonomously until a defined completion point. The new version automatically thinks before replying, eliminating the need for explicit prompts to do so, and provides clear summaries of its actions during long runs.

The update includes guidance on how to prompt Opus 5.5 effectively, such as specifying what "done" looks like for a task and when to stop and ask for input. It also supports adding instructions mid-run and managing design preferences by naming unwanted styles. For developers using Claude Code, the model can be steered with rules about when to pause for user input and can distribute large tasks across subagents for parallel processing, improving efficiency and oversight.

It balances model capability and deployment cost, allowing efficient on-premise use without sending data to third parties. Aleph Alpha emphasizes full supply-chain transparency and intellectual property safety to ensure compliance and sovereignty for its customers. The company also developed internal evaluation suites tailored to sector-specific requirements, improving performance on real-world tasks beyond public benchmarks.

items.originalTitle: Can AI self-improvement overcome diminishing returns?
items.summary:
The article examines whether AI's ability to improve itself autonomously, known as recursive self-improvement (RSI), is sufficient to cause a rapid surge to artificial superintelligence (ASI). It argues that current evidence indicates the self-improvement feedback loop is too weak to sustain exponential growth leading to ASI, suggesting progress will be rapid but not explosive.

The author categorizes different types of AI self-improvement and notes that while narrow superintelligence exists in specific domains like game playing and formal math, broader autonomous self-improvement has not yet demonstrated accelerating returns. The analysis calls for more data to better understand AI progress and remains open to breakthroughs that could alter this assessment.

items.title: OpenAI’s AI model solves a weaker version of the Navier–Stokes problem but experts say mathematicians remain essential for conceptual breakthroughs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
items.originalTitle: AI will not make mathematicians obsolete
items.summary:
OpenAI announced that an internal AI model solved a weaker form of the Navier–Stokes problem, a century-old question in fluid dynamics, marking the second Clay Millennium Prize Problem addressed by AI. The solution involved adding an artificial external force to the equations, a condition allowed by a previous formulation but not representative of the original unforced problem.

Experts note that while AI can find complex examples through exhaustive search, it has not yet tackled the core conceptual challenges that define mathematical research. The creative and conceptual aspects of mathematics, such as choosing meaningful problems and interpreting results, remain reliant on human insight, ensuring that mathematicians continue to play a vital role despite AI’s computational advances.
